Dear Sir or Madam.
am replying for Mr. Tom Culp, the General Manager of our newspapers, in my capacity of Publisher and President of the corporation.
Subject: Droft Environmental Statement re Executive Order 11644
Basically, it is my opinion that the draft is well-executed and probably as complete as possible, given t'e "state-of-the-ard" that now exists regarding accommodation of motorcycles and other off-read recreation vehicles in the natural environment. There are, however, some points of confusion and one or two omissions that I think should be clarified in the final draft.
In paragraph I-1.-b)-(i)-(b) where it says "... no person shall operate an OhV in Interior lands: In excess of established speed limits;" I think that some clarification should be provided to make it known that not all Interior lands would be limited as to speed, that speed limits, where posted, would be indicated for causing areas, parking lots, trail intersections, etc. as needed. Where speed limits are not needed (most places), the only limit should be what speed is safe for the conditions and skill of the operator. Certainly there should be no speed limits applied to organized racing events.
In this same section on Operating Criteria, I think that you should add a paragraph (iv) stating that no person shall operate an Oli on Interior laids which produces visible emission. In other words, cars, motorcycles, snow-burnies, etc. should not emit smoke that can be seen. This requirement would not six be difficult to enforce and the reasons for it should be obvious. Compliance would be easy, also, for there are many "smokeless" lubricants on the market.
In the following paragraph XI (iv-3), the sentence regarding bonds or deposits posted by the permittee should be amended to read "... money in such amounts as may be reasonably required to cover costs of restoration, [etc.]"
